Erst or Nur? German A2 Time and Quantity Practice

Distinguish not until/only so far with erst from a simple limitation with nur. Practise time expectations, age and quantity cues.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions + writing task

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Try the exercisesWrite your own sentence

Understand the difference

Nur limits an amount or excludes alternatives: Ich möchte nur Wasser. Erst can mean not until with a time, or only so far relative to a later expectation: Der Zug fährt erst um zehn; ich habe erst zwei Seiten gelesen. Meaning and speaker expectations matter, not just the English word only.

Common mistake to avoid

Erst zwei Seiten and nur zwei Seiten can both be grammatical. Erst often suggests more remains or is expected, while nur stresses the limited amount.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Compare the meaning and sentence pattern, rather than choosing by English translation alone.

Worked example 1Der Kurs beginnt erst nächste Woche.The course does not begin until next week.
Worked example 2Ich möchte nur ein Glas Leitungswasser.I would like only a glass of tap water.
Worked example 3Wir haben erst den ersten Abschnitt geschafft.We have only completed the first section so far.
Worked example 4Im kleinen Rucksack ist nur Platz für eine Jacke.There is room for only one jacket in the small backpack.

Practice: choose the right word

Use erst for not until/only so far and nur for the stated limitation or exclusion. Follow the meaning cue. Try each question before opening the answer. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Der Bus kommt ___ um elf, nicht schon um zehn. (not until)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: erst

Erst marks a later-than-expected or specified starting point.

Question 2. Ich trinke heute ___ Wasser, keinen Saft. (exclusion)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: nur

Nur excludes the alternative juice.

Question 3. Von zehn Aufgaben habe ich ___ zwei erledigt. (only so far)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: erst

Erst presents two as progress so far; nur would stress the small total.

Question 4. Bitte pack ___ die blauen Hefte ein, keine anderen. (exclusion)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: nur

Nur restricts the choice to the blue exercise books.

Use it in your own sentence

Contrast wanting water only with a bus leaving as late as ten.

Try writing your answer before reading the model below. Other natural answers are possible.

One possible answer

Ich möchte nur Wasser. Der Bus fährt erst um zehn.

Check your wording: Nur limits the choice; erst presents the time as later than expected.

What to practise next

Write a new context for each word. Explain which meaning or object pattern makes your choice natural; some contexts allow both.

Try the gaps again on another day without reading the explanation first. If a choice is still unclear, use the linked grammar foundation before moving to another topic.
